terms.grammar: phrase: mandāre with the dative memoriae
evidence: Cic. Lael. 1.3: ejus disputātiōnis sententiās memoriae mandāvī (Lewis & Short s.v. is)
terms.comment: Cicero’s phrase for “commit to memory”: memoriae mandāre, to hand over to the memory. Ēdiscere is to learn a text off by heart.

terms.gloss: hold in the memory, commit to memory
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.154 (Lewis & Short s.v. memoria)
Traupman 103: to commit to memory, memoriae committere
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase, an English calque that Lewis & Short does not quote; Cicero says memoriae mandāre (above).

sources: Lewis & Short: edisco
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 30, 97, 103, 338.
Lewis & Short: memoria · Lewis & Short: mando
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
